transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I feel like there’s something going on behind the scenes on my jobs, like people are plotting around my designs, and no one can convince me otherwise. My husband tries to tell me I'm imagining it, but I know they are secretly working together to push me out.
Have you experienced any periods where these beliefs about people plotting against you went away for a while, or have they been consistently present over time?

They’ve been pretty consistent for most of this past year, and even when they quiet down a little, they never truly go away. Even late last summer when my energy picked up and I felt a bit less weighed down, I was still absolutely convinced people were emailing behind my back to ruin my designs. It just always seems to be there in the background.
Can you describe a specific situation where your belief about people plotting against you led to a significant change in your behavior or caused you significant distress, and how you responded to it?

On job sites, I get so paranoid that the builders and homeowners are secretly emailing to sabotage my layouts that I'll freeze in the middle of a room or pace around checking the windows, convinced we're being watched. Even when my husband shows me normal contracts to prove me wrong, I'm certain there's a secret email chain laughing at me, and this distress has caused me to make mistakes and lose major clients.
Have you ever experienced any bizarre or unreal hallucinations, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, in addition to your beliefs about people plotting against you?

Yes, when I’m alone on job sites laying tile or sketching, I hear a man's voice right behind me saying things like, "You’re messing it up again" or "They all know you’re a fraud." There is absolutely no one else in the room, but it sounds so clear and real that it completely shakes me up.
Can you tell me more about when you hear the voice, is it only when you're thinking about the plots against you or does it happen at other times as well?

It mostly happens when I'm alone working on a site, laying tile or sketching, rather than just when I'm actively focusing on the plots. The voice says things like "You're messing it up again" or "They all know you're a fraud," which often happens concurrently when I'm feeling extremely low and convinced they are plotting against me. Still, it can really happen anytime I'm alone in an empty house trying to get my work done.
Can you describe if there are times when the voice you hear and your beliefs about people plotting against you seem to be connected, or if they feel like separate experiences?

They feel very closely connected to me because they usually happen at the same time when I'm on a job site. When the voice whispers that "they all know" I'm a fraud, it directly feeds into my belief that the builders are secretly emailing each other to sabotage my designs. Even during times when my mood was a bit better, both the voice and the feeling of being plotted against were still happening right alongside each other.

Have you noticed any significant disorganization in your thoughts, such as difficulty maintaining a logical flow of ideas, or any bizarre behaviors that are not typical of you, especially when the voice is present or when you're feeling extremely convinced of the plots against you?

Yes, my husband and clients say I jump all over the place when I talk, like shifting from a flooring estimate to theater ideas or my pastor's sermon without realizing it. I've also had times on site where I just freeze for long stretches holding a tile or trowel, or pace around muttering and checking the windows because I feel like we're being watched.

Can you tell me more about how often these episodes of disorganized thinking and freezing or pacing happen, and if they seem to be triggered by anything in particular, such as the voice or your beliefs about plots against you?

The jumping between topics usually happens when I'm trying to talk to my husband or clients, while the freezing and pacing mostly occur on days when I'm working on a job site. I don't know if there is a direct trigger, but these episodes definitely happen in those same high-stress environments where I hear the voice criticizing me and feel overwhelmed by the belief that others are plotting against me.

Can you estimate how often these episodes of disorganized thinking, such as jumping between topics or freezing and pacing, occur in a typical week, and do they seem to worsen or improve when the voice is more prominent or when your beliefs about plots against you are more intense?

I definitely experience those moments of jumping between topics, freezing, and pacing, but I'm really not sure of the exact number of times they happen in a typical week. I also can't tell if they directly change in intensity based on the voices or the paranoid thoughts, as it all just feels like a blur when it's happening.

Have you experienced any significant periods of elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep that lasted for several days or more, especially in relation to your episodes of disorganized thinking or the presence of the voice?

No, I’ve never had any periods of feeling high or not needing sleep—most of the time over this past year, I've felt completely exhausted, low, and drained. There was a brief time late last summer where I felt slightly less weighed down and my energy picked up a little, but it wasn't an elevated state, and I was still dealing with the voice and the paranoia.

Have you ever experienced any periods of feeling extremely irritable, restless, or easily annoyed, which might not be directly related to your beliefs about people plotting against you or the voice you hear?

No, I don't think I've ever had periods of feeling really irritable or restless separate from those worries. Whenever I do feel tense or on edge, it is always because of the voice criticizing me or because I'm so stressed about people plotting behind my back.

Can you tell me if there are times when the voice you hear and your beliefs about plots seem to overwhelm you to the point where you have difficulty distinguishing what's real and what's not, or if you're always able to maintain some awareness that these experiences might not be based in reality?

They feel completely real to me, and in those moments, it's impossible to maintain any awareness that they might not be real. Even when my husband shows me normal contracts to prove otherwise, I still can't shake the belief that there is a secret email chain plotting against me. The voice sounds so clear and right behind me that I am absolutely convinced it is happening.
Can you think of any situation or evidence that could possibly convince you that the plots against you are not real, or do you feel that no matter what, these beliefs will always be true to you?

It really feels impossible to convince me otherwise because the feeling is just too strong. Even when my husband shows me normal messages and contracts to prove nothing is wrong, I still feel convinced there is a secret, separate email chain I’m not allowed to see. I just know they are using it to laugh at me and plan to push me out of the business.
Do you ever have moments where you question the reality of the voice or the plots against you, or do you always believe they are real and happening?

I always believe they are completely real, and I don't have moments where I question them. Even when my husband shows me normal emails or I look around to see that a room is completely empty, I still feel absolutely certain that the plots and the voice are happening. It is just a reality to me, and I cannot be convinced otherwise.

Can you think of any times when you were able to consider the possibility that your beliefs about people plotting against you might not be true, even if just for a moment, or has this never happened to you?

No, that has never happened to me; I have never been able to doubt those thoughts. Even when my husband shows me normal messages or contracts to prove otherwise, I remain firmly convinced there is a hidden, separate email chain I'm not allowed to see. No one can convince me otherwise because it just feels entirely real.

Do you think it's possible that your experiences, including the voice and the plots against you, could be a product of your own mind rather than actual events happening in the world, or do you believe they are definitely real and happening outside of your thoughts?

I know my husband and others tell me these things are just in my head, but they feel completely and undeniably real to me. The voice and the plots feel like they are definitely happening out in the real world, and it is impossible for me to see them as just being in my mind. It causes me so much distress, but I just can't shake the reality of it.

Can you think of any difference between the times when you hear the voice and when you believe people are plotting against you, in terms of how real they feel to you, or do they both feel equally real?

I haven't really thought about it that way because they both feel completely and terrifyingly real to me. I can't really tell a difference in how real they feel, as they both just seem like absolute reality when they are happening.
Can you describe if the voice you hear ever comments on your thoughts or actions as they are happening, or if it mainly focuses on criticizing you or talking about the plots against you?

Yes, the voice definitely comments on my actions as they are happening, especially to criticize me while I'm trying to work. For instance, when I am laying tile or sketching a layout, it will say "You're messing it up again" or tell me that everyone knows I'm a fraud.
Can you tell me if the voice you hear ever tells you to do specific actions or commands you to perform certain tasks, or is it primarily critical or commenting on your actions?

No, the voice never commands me to do anything or tells me to perform specific tasks. It is always just critical, whispering right behind me while I'm working and saying things like "You're messing it up again" or "They all know you're a fraud."
Have you ever experienced any voices telling you to harm yourself or others, in addition to the critical comments you've mentioned?

No, the voice has never told me to hurt myself or anyone else; it only criticizes my designs and calls me a fraud. I do sometimes have my own dark thoughts of wishing I wouldn't wake up or picturing driving my truck off the highway, but those are just my own feelings and not the voice commanding me to do it.

Can you describe if the voice you hear and your beliefs about plots against you have ever led to any significant changes in your daily life or relationships, such as avoiding certain places or people due to your fears?

Yes, they have completely disrupted my life and relationships; I've pulled away from my friends and stopped going to the community theater entirely. On job sites, the fear of people plotting and the voice calling me a fraud have led to missed appointments, half-finished jobs, and losing major clients. It has gotten so overwhelming that my husband has had to take over managing the bills and the household because I just can't handle things anymore.

Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you had delusions or hallucinations without a major depressive or manic episode, or have these experiences always been accompanied by significant mood symptoms?

Yes, late last summer there was a period of a few weeks where my mood lifted slightly, my energy and appetite improved, and I felt less weighed down. However, even though I felt better emotionally during that time, the paranoia about people emailing behind my back and the critical voice on job sites remained just as strong.

Can you estimate how often the episodes of disorganized thinking, such as jumping between topics or freezing and pacing, occur in relation to the times when you hear the critical voice or feel strongly that people are plotting against you?

I'm really not sure how to track or compare the timing of those two things. When it's happening, everything just feels like a blur, and I haven't really thought about how they line up chronologically.
Can you describe any times when your thoughts felt so disorganized or confusing that you had trouble understanding yourself or making sense of what was happening around you?

Yes, that happens to me a lot. My husband and clients tell me I jump all over the place when I'm talking; for example, I'll start explaining a flooring estimate and then suddenly go off about the theater director stealing my scene ideas or my pastor's sermon. I can see from their faces that they are completely lost, but I just can't seem to pull my thoughts back to the original point.
Can you think of any times when the voice you hear and your disorganized thinking, such as jumping between topics, happened at the same time, or were they separate experiences?

I'm not quite sure, and I haven't really thought about whether they happen at the exact same moment. But both the voice and the jumping between topics have been happening to me during this same difficult period over the last year.

Can you describe if there are any times when you feel like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by an outside force, or if you've ever felt like you're being forced to think certain thoughts against your will?

No, I don't feel like an outside force is controlling my thoughts or forcing me to think things against my will. Even though I get completely overwhelmed by my own worries, the voice I hear, and the feeling that people are plotting against me, my thoughts still feel like my own.
Have you ever felt like the voice you hear is controlling your thoughts or actions, or is it more of a commentary on what you're doing?

No, the voice doesn't control my thoughts or actions at all; it is definitely more of a constant, critical commentary. It just criticizes my work and character while I'm working alone on job sites, repeating things like "You're messing it up again" or "They all know you're a fraud."
Can you describe if the voice you hear and your beliefs about plots against you have changed in intensity or nature over time, or have they remained relatively consistent?

They have been very consistent and a regular part of my life for most of this past year. Even late last summer when my mood and energy improved slightly, the voice criticizing me and the belief that people were plotting against me remained just as intense and did not go away. They haven't really changed in nature; they just stay constantly there in the background.
Have you ever experienced any other types of hallucinations, such as seeing things that aren't there, in addition to hearing the critical voice?
No, I have never seen things that aren't actually there. It has only ever been that man's voice whispering right behind me and criticizing my work when I'm alone.
Can you describe if the voice you hear is always commenting on your actions or thoughts, or if there are times when it seems to be having a conversation with you or responding to your thoughts?

No, it doesn't really engage in a back-and-forth conversation with me or respond to my thoughts. Instead, it just feels like a man standing right behind me and judging what I'm doing, saying things like "You're messing it up again" or "They all know you're a fraud" while I try to work.
